L147@P2: 2. The run theorem
L148@P2: 2.1. Basic definitions
L149@P2: Here we give the definitions for some of the basic concepts of this paper, including descent
L150@P2: compositions and noncommutative symmetric functions.
L151@P2: Given a permutation π in Sn, we say that i ∈ [n − 1] is a descent of π if πi > πi+1.
L152@P2: Then, increasing runs of π can be characterized as maximal consecutive subsequences of π
L153@P2: containing no descents. Let us call an increasing run short if it has length 1, and long if it
L154@P2: has length at least 2.
L155@P2: The number of increasing runs of a nonempty permutation is one more than its number
L156@P2: of descents; in fact, the lengths of the increasing runs determine the descents, and vice versa.
L157@P2: Given a subset S ⊆ [n − 1] with elements s1 < s2 < · · · < sj, let C(S) be the composition
L158@P2: (s1, s2 − s1, . . . , sj − sj−1, n − sj ) of n, and given a composition L = (L1, L2, . . . , Lk), let
L159@P2: D(L) = {L1, L1 + L2, . . . , L1 + · · · + Lk−1} be the corresponding subset of [n − 1]. Then,
L160@P2: C and D are inverse bijections. If π is a permutation with descent set S, we call C(S) the
L161@P2: descent composition of π, which give the lengths of the increasing runs of π. Applying D to
L162@P2: the descent composition of a permutation gives its descent set.
L163@P2: The definitions and properties of descents, increasing runs, and descent compositions
L164@P2: extend naturally to words in the free monoid on any totally ordered alphabet such as [n] or
L165@P2: P. Note that increasing runs in words are allowed to be weakly increasing, whereas increasing
L166@P2: runs in permutations are necessarily strictly increasing since no letters repeat.

L289@P4: To obtain (1.2), we define a variant of descents and increasing runs as follows. Given
L290@P4: a permutation π in Sn, we say that i ∈ [n − 1] is an alternating descent of π if i is odd
L291@P4: and πi > πi+1 or if i is even and πi < πi+1. Similarly, an alternating run of π is a maximal
L292@P4: consecutive subsequence of π containing no alternating descents, and we can also define
L293@P4: alternating descent sets and alternating descent compositions analogously.
